units.translation: For I say that a combination of words is a most shameful disease.
I would be sick, if it is a disease to hate one's enemies.
disease
disease.
Improperly of the earth being shaken
Of the earth not bearing crops
Of those fleeing
Of a condition of the mind
Having fallen into disease.
If someone should fall into disease.
They ward off all diseases.
How was this not a disease of the mind that held my child?
You were then in possession of this delightful disease.
For disease—a neighbor sharing the same wall presses upon us.
The diseases of us two.
And white temples rise up with this disease.
The water of the Nile, untouched by diseases.
And a joyless swarm of diseases from the citizens would settle on the head. This is the only example of the Ionic form, perhaps introduced by a scribe, since the meter requires νόσων.
And inexperienced in diseases.
And the sea-shaking trident, a disease of the earth.
Let no fruitless, grievous disease creep upon us.

Gods, casting upon those outside the walls a man-destroying disease, a shield-casting ruin, may you win glory for these citizens, where I have corrected νόσον, ῥίψοπλον for καταρίψοπλον, which M has from the first hand, changed by another ancient hand to καὶ τὰν ῥίψοπλον. καὶ τὰν is not a corruption of νόσον, but is the work of an interpolator clumsily supplying two missing syllables.
For who could have stopped the treacherous diseases of Hera?
Having found what kind of remedy for this disease?
Allow me to be sick with this disease.
You have named a god-sent disease.
What is the remedy for the disease?
Let us first inquire into this disease.
I hear that you are raving with no small disease.
And there is no disease which I have spat upon more than this one.
A burden doubles the disease for the one who possesses it.
We shall try to avert the pain of the disease.
Fasting destroyed the disease.
A piercing ruin carries the guilty one to abound in disease (this is corrupt).
An unbearable, grievous disease.

pertaining to return
pertaining to return.
returning
Unexpectedly I see the light of return.
The army will obtain the safety of return.
For it is necessary for the house to have the safety of return.
He seems to rejoice in the safety of return.
I learn about Menelaus whether he is returning (γε M, which L. Dindorf corrected in the Thesaurus vol. 5 p. 1573) and saved will come back with you.
return
return.
And about the royal return.
And returns from wars brought them home without toil.
I shall send you a voice of ill omen, a greeting for your return.
Those who are responsible for my return.
I learn of the return from their eyes.
to deprive
to deprive.
Passive Choephori 491
Having deprived Nisus of his immortal lock.
Of one who deprives someone of life, Septem 982 ANT. He destroyed this (the breath). IS. And he deprived him of it.
Then may I perish, having deprived.
Of a woman who deprives her husband.
without
without.
A word frequent in epic poetry, very rare in Attic poetry, of which there is one example in Aeschylus, Supplices 239 νόσφιν ἡγητῶν [without leaders].
of deprivations
faulty in M Prometheus 459 for σοφισμάτων.
of clever devices
